newsitem.title: PERU: British Steel unit plans LatAm expansion.
newsitem.headline: British Steel unit plans LatAm expansion.

text.p: British Steel Track Products Ltd, a unit of British Steel Plc that supplies rails and railway infrastructure, plans to expand its business in Latin America, a company official said.
"The privatization process is gathering pace in the region, which creates a better business climate for investment," the company's commercial manager Stewart Askew told a press conference.

The economic climate in Latin America is good for new railroad projects, such as the Ferronorte project in Brazil, La Loma coal project in Colombia, and plans in Paraguay to lay 134 miles (215 kms) of lines between Concepcion and Ponta Pora in Brazil, Askew said.

He said the British rail company, which produces 250,000 tonnes of rails annually, plans to sell 10,000 to 15,000 tonnes this year to Latin America, up from 6,000 tonnes in 1996. The total last year stemmed from a $3 million contract to supply rails to Peruvian state-owned Empresa Nacional de Ferrocarriles (Enafer), he added.
The company recently signed a letter of intent to supply 15,000 tonnes of rails to Brazil's Sao Paulo subway, another company official said.
In the region, British Steel has worked on Mexican railroads, the Rio de Janeiro subway, the Carrejon project in Colombia and on several Chilean mining projects, among others, he said.
"In the future we want to see the Latin American market contributing to our general business in marketing performance, providing this is based on sound financial principles," Askew said.
